docs.title: Grid Destruction
docs.text:
Server-authoritative destructible walls for Unreal Engine 5 multiplayer.

Shoot a wall and a hole appears in real geometry. Bullets, grenades and players pass through it, and every client sees the identical hole.

This is not decals, a swapped-out "broken" mesh or client-side cosmetics. The server owns the wall's state, and everything else follows from it: the surface, the collider, the structural collapse and the debris.

Quick start Wire your weapons

The showcase level: a glazed wall blows out, then a room loses its walls and the roof comes down.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text: Feature What it means Real holes A procedural surface rebuilt from cell state. Craters go the full depth of the wall, rims show its real thickness, and edges chip at the subdivision's own resolution rather than smearing. Matching collision The collider carries the same holes as the mesh, so what you can see through, you can shoot and walk through. Replication you can verify Only damaged cells replicate, budgeted to stay under the engine's limits, and clients never author damage. Each client checks its walls against a hash the server publishes and heals itself on a mismatch. GridDestruction.HashCells prints its own MATCH / MISMATCH verdict. Adaptive detail Fine detail exists only where the wall has been shot, so an untouched wall costs what a coarse grid costs. Per-material behaviour Concrete, brick, stone, wood, metal and glass differ in penetration, spall, edge crumble, debris weight and grazing response. Glass is whole or gone. Every number is a documented preset field, and all of them live in one CSV table. Every side breaks A shot on a top cap, an end or a window jamb cuts that side along its own normal, and the bore of a hole widens as it is shot through. Joined walls Walls that meet at a corner or end to end find each other. The seam disappears, a hit crosses the joint, and pieces hold each other up only through real ground. Structural collapse Detached pieces fall as rubble with the weight of their material. A ceiling rests on the walls below it, and an overhang longer than the material can carry gives way. Authored break patterns A mask, or the height map of the wall's own material. Brick cracks along its mortar joints. A ready damage material Dents read as chips and cracks with parallax depth, holes get cracks and dust, and broken rims show the inside of the material. An intact wall looks exactly like its textures. Effects and sounds Break, collapse, landing and dust effects and sounds fire per material, from the side the piece came off, with no Blueprint wiring. Level-building tools Walls sized in centimetres, built by clicks, resized with viewport handles, grouped into kits. Window and door openings are cut live in the editor. Walls are part of the navmesh. Saved damage (beta) Capture a wall's damage as an asset for pre-damaged buildings, or as a struct your save game carries. Physical materials on the collider Your existing impact decals and surface-type logic answer correctly against a destructible wall.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Unreal Engine 5.7 or 5.8, Win64.
  • A C++ project, or the Fab binaries for a Blueprint-only project.
  • The ProceduralMeshComponent and Niagara engine plugins. Both are declared as dependencies, and the editor enables them for you.

The Core module has no dependency on Lyra, on the Gameplay Ability System or on anything but the engine. The plugin has been tested in a blank project and in a Lyra Starter Game copy, as a listen server and as a dedicated server, with clients on the same PC and on a second PC.

docs.title: Not in this version
docs.text:
• Walls are planar. Curved and cylindrical sections are on the roadmap.
  • Built and tested against Unreal Engine 5.7 and 5.8, on Win64.
  • The shipped damage material is one generic look (cracks, chips, dust). The data under it is documented channel by channel, for a material of your own.
  • A late joiner receives each wall's damaged cells in one update, which the engine caps at about 64 KB. A very large wall at the highest subdivision can exceed that when fully destroyed. Such walls get a warning at start, and Multiplayer lists the ways out.
  • Saved damage is beta: it works, but the capture workflow is still rough.

First release, for Unreal Engine 5.7 and 5.8 on Win64.

Destruction

  • Grid destruction with adaptive detail, a procedural surface and a matching procedural collider.
  • Side erosion of caps, ends, window jambs and the bore of a hole; corners chip before faces dent; dents drawn in whole chips.
  • Exit blowout on the far face; glancing hits leave furrows; grazing and ricochet response per material.
  • Brittle glass that breaks in whole shards.
  • Break patterns from a mask or from the wall material's own height map.

Structure

  • Structural collapse with falling rubble weighted by the physical material.
  • Joined walls: shared seams, hits that cross a joint, support only through real ground. Floors and ceilings that rest on walls; an overhang limit, with a choice of how overhangs built into a level behave.
  • Layered walls whose inner faces take no blowout.

Multiplayer

  • Server-authoritative. Only damaged cells replicate, budgeted to stay under the engine's limits.
  • Published per-wall hash, client desync detection and automatic resend; GridNetClientComponent for an immediate resend and an on-screen net panel.
  • GridDestruction.HashCells with its own MATCH / MISMATCH verdict; GridNet.Measure for bandwidth.
  • Late-join size warning.

Look

  • Six material presets (concrete, brick, stone, wood, metal, glass) and a thin concrete variant, all driven by one CSV table.
  • Damage vertex channels and a wall-normalised UV set on every wall mesh.
  • M_Grid_DamageWall damage material and two material functions for your own materials.
  • Niagara effects and sounds per material, fired by the wall, with no Blueprint wiring.

Tools

  • Walls sized in centimetres, click building, viewport handles, wall variants and kits, live openings, texture placement controls.
  • Walls in the navmesh, with breaches walkable under a dynamic navmesh.
  • Damage snapshots for pre-damaged levels and save games (beta).
  • Sample wall pieces and four kits in Variants/, ready for the build arrows' right-click menu.
  • A showcase level and a third-person sample character with a rifle, a breaching charge, a cutter and a thrown grenade.
  • Blueprint integration with no dependencies (Apply Grid Damage) or through a GameplayTag weapon table (Notify Hit By Tag).

docs.title: Damage material
docs.text:
The plugin ships a wall material that draws damage in the shader:

  • chips with parallax depth inside dents;
  • cracks spreading from dents and holes;
  • the material's interior on broken rims;
  • dust around holes.

It reads everything from vertex data the wall mesh already carries, so:

  • nothing travels over the network, and a player who joins mid-match sees the same wall;
  • nothing is computed on the CPU when a wall is hit;
  • an intact wall looks exactly like its textures.

Cost: three texture reads and about 40 ALU instructions per pixel of wall. No extra draw calls.

docs.title: What ships
docs.text:
In /GridDestruction/Materials/:

asset what it is M_Grid_DamageWall a complete wall material; make instances of it MF_GridDamageUV function: UV → FaceUV with the parallax offset, and DetailUV MF_GridDamage function: your BaseColor, Roughness and Normal → the same with damage, plus AO T_Grid_DamageDetail, T_Grid_DamageDetail_N the crack and chip texture and its normal map MI_Grid_Damage_Brick, _Concrete, _Stone, _Wood, _Metal, _Glass demo instances with tuned values and placeholder textures in Materials/Surfaces/

The shipped GP_* presets already use the demo instances, and the CSV's FractureWeightMask row gives brick, stone and wood their placeholder height maps as the break pattern.

docs.title: Make an instance for your surface
docs.text:
1. Right-click M_Grid_DamageWall → Create Material Instance. Save it in your own project, for example /Game/Materials/MI_Brick_Damage, not in the plugin's Content, so a plugin update never overwrites it.
  2. Open the instance. Under Parameter Groups you see Surface and Grid Damage. A parameter stays grey until you tick the box to the left of its name; unticked, the instance takes the parent's value.
  3. Set the Surface group (below), save with Ctrl+S. The preview and the walls in the level update at once.

You need one instance per wall material: MI_Brick_Damage, MI_Concrete_Damage and so on.

docs.title: Surface group
docs.text:
parameter what to set BaseColorMap the albedo, for example of your brick. sRGB on, like any colour texture NormalMap the normal map. Its texture must have Compression = Normalmap, or the parameter reports a sampler type error BaseTint a colour multiplier. White by default: the texture as it is Roughness one number: brick 0.85–0.9, concrete 0.9. For a roughness map, use the functions instead (below) UVTiling the number your old material multiplied TexCoord by. If it used TexCoord directly, leave 1 DamagedColorMap optional. A texture of the broken material: bare brick without patina, concrete with exposed aggregate, fresh wood. Shown in the damaged area and on rims when DamagedMapAmount > 0 DamagedNormalMap optional. The normal map for DamagedColorMap, Compression = Normalmap, so the relief changes too

Check

On an intact wall the instance must look exactly like your old material. If it does not, the Surface group is set wrong; the damage part has nothing to do with it.

docs.title: Put it on the walls
docs.text:
Through the CSV, so the value is not lost: write the instance's path in the WallMaterial row of the right column of GridMaterials.csv and run the table script (Surface presets).

Without the CSV: put the instance in the preset's WallMaterial and press Apply Preset.

Not on the actor

A material assigned on the wall actor is overwritten by the preset the next time it is applied. GridDestruction.CheckPresets should print MATCH.

bEmitDamageAttributes on the wall's GridWallMesh component is on by default. If nothing reacts to hits, check it on the placed actor, not the class.

docs.title: Tuning without PIE
docs.text:
1. Shoot a wall in PIE and run GridDestruction.CaptureDamage to save its damage into a damage preset (Setup → saved damage).
  2. Place a test wall with that preset as its Initial Damage. The editor viewport shows it damaged.
  3. Open the instance next to the wall and turn the parameters: changes show at once.

It helps to have light dents, a deep crater and a hole through on one preset.

docs.title: Grid Damage parameters, in tuning order
a) Crack scale: DetailTiling (default 2)
docs.text:
Crack tile size = UV Tile Cm / (UVTiling × DetailTiling). With a 100 cm UV tile and UVTiling 1 the tile is 50 cm: a crack network cell of about 11 cm and chips of 2–4 cm.

  • For brick use 2–3, so cracks are in scale with the bricks.
  • If you see a repeating pattern, use a non-integer such as 2.37, so it does not line up with the brick tile.

docs.title: b) When chips appear: DentGain (default 4)
docs.text:
Chips show fully once 1 / DentGain of the thickness is gone. The rule:

DentGain ≈ ThicknessCm / the dent depth in cm at which chips should show fully

For full chips at a 4 cm dent:

material thickness DentGain brick 20 5 concrete 25 6 stone 40 10 wood 8 2

A good target: one bullet leaves visible but not solid chipping.

docs.title: c) Cracks from holes: BreachCracks (default 1), with BreachFalloffCells
docs.text:
• BreachFalloffCells on the preset (brick: 2.5 cells) sets how far the zone around a hole reaches.
  • BreachCracks sets how densely cracks fill it: 1.5–2 for more cracks at the edge, 0 for cracks only inside dents.
  • To make cracks reach further from a hole, change BreachFalloffCells in the CSV, not the material.

docs.title: d) The damaged area: DamageTint, AreaSoftness, DamagedMapAmount
docs.text:
A dent is coloured as one patch, and the patch's edge is:

  • ragged and chipped, like knocked-off plaster, not the shape of the cells;
  • sharp, a pixel wide at any distance: neither blurry up close nor stepped far away;
  • sometimes stopped by cracks, where the breakup is lower.
parameter default what it does DamageTint 0.8, 0.75, 0.72 colour multiplier inside the patch. Lower is darker and more visible; 1, 1, 1 turns the patch off AreaSoftness 1.5 edge width in pixels: 1 is sharpest, 3–4 softer. Below 1 it may shimmer far away DamagedMapAmount 0 0: the patch and rims use the face texture, tinted. 1: they show the broken material (DamagedColorMap, DamagedNormalMap, DamagedRoughness). The demo instances use 1 DamagedRoughness 0.95 roughness of the broken material

Rims (caps and opening reveals) look exactly like the face material on an intact wall. The broken material appears on a rim only as it is damaged: at the edge of a hole through, and where a side hit chipped the rim.

Intact and broken in one material. The patch grows with the cell's damage: the deeper the damage, the more of the surface becomes the broken material. It works like two instances, intact and broken, blended by the damage mask, but in one material and one pass. Hits shallower than DentStepCm leave the geometry flat and show only here.

If you cannot see the patch, light dents are too shallow for DentGain: raise DentGain or darken DamageTint.

docs.title: e) Colours
docs.text: parameter what it does CrackColor crack colour, near black; dark brown for brick ChipTint multiplies the surface colour inside a chip. Below 1 gives shadow and a sense of depth InteriorTint multiplies the surface colour on a hole's rims. Can go above 1: a fresh break is lighter than the surface DustAmount, DustTint dust around holes. Its colour is the average colour of the texture × DustTint (slightly lighter by default: 1.15, 1.12, 1.08). The master material reads the average from the smallest mip of BaseColorMap, so dust always matches the material

docs.title: f) Depth: ParallaxDepth (default 0.02), tune last
docs.text:
An offset in fractions of the face tile: 0.02 on a 100 cm tile is about 2 cm at grazing angles.

  • Check it by walking along the wall at a sharp angle. If the texture inside chips swims, lower it.
  • Working range 0.01–0.04; 0 turns parallax off.

docs.title: g) Relief: NormalStrength (default 1)
docs.text: Concrete and stone 1.2–1.5, brick 1.

docs.text:
